Two things I wanted to run by the community:

  1. Should we have a game wipe when we finish the rules?

  2. Should we have a thread for minor fixes such as flair or map color issues?

We'd appreciate your input.

If wipe includes bringing countries back to their original size and nullifying annexations and such, I'd vote no. Mostly because I've seen many (and me) who've put time into expanding their country meticulously and waited the time required. Same for alliances and such, it'd be a bit sad if all those went to waste. But I definitely support trying to figure something out like a ''check in and be active at least every other day'' or so, to make sure we actually know who's active and who's not. It's a bit sad otherwise. And, the second thread would be handy. Even though, if it's fine for the mods, the either private request or META thread on a case by case basis could work.

I understand the reluctance of accepting a wipe. I myself have beta tested many projects, games, whatever. However I find that they generally result in a more fulfilling and fun experience in the end. Unless everything g just breaks, it would not happen for another irl month, at least. (also excluding a high community demand for one.)

Currently our tentative, proposed, rule on inactivity is one week. However without automation (which we need voat bot support for) it is very difficult to keep track of that. (in fact it's hard to keep track of anything)

The reason for the thread I'm suggesting is because it'd be vastly easier for us mods to keep track of all the revelation data and threads so we can make an informed decision in case the players reach a stalemate.

We can involve the community in identifying inactive players. We can have a thread or something to name them, and if anybody spots one, they'll say who it is. That way we don't have to have it as a weekly thing. Regarding the wipe, we can just see there and then, whether everyone'd be fine with it, and with declaring the game so far as simply a test and not the real thing. Could work.

Until we have bots, a thread might be a good idea. We could definitely use community help whenever possible.

As far as the wipe, we aren't planning for it in the near future, and we would have at least a week notice. During that week we would be open to further community discussion on it.

I don't think a game wipe is necessary at this point, things are just starting to get interesting and if we wipe it then I think a lot of people would lose interest. Forming Byzantium from Romania took a fair bit of maneuvering so I don't think I could pull it off again.

Well as I commented earlier, a wipe is purely in the hypothetical stage.

You could almost consider the current "game" (read:subverse) as an alpha state. It won't be complete until we have semi-finalized rules, a solid system of handling conflicts, and bot powered automation.

At least one of these things is likely to take at least three months, real time.
I get that, totally. Perhaps we could do a surveymonkey poll prior to the wipe and have the majority decide.

That's an excellent idea. Our goal will always be to run this subverse on what the community feels is best. We're just trying to use our programming and management skills to facilitate : our goal is always to have the community in charge.

If/when we do a wipe I think we should maybe have a short period of claims only to start out. I'd also be in favor of stricter rules on expansion especially in the beginning. I think perhaps people might be a bit turned off after a lot of the major nations have been picked up just by expansion. Maybe allow newcomers to claim annexed nations through revolt (maybe even allow that now without wiping). Maybe require nations to be sufficiently larger in terms of population/GDP/area than the area you're annexing.

Right now I think some of the role play is a little thin with a lot of the annexing going on. It's a bit unconvincing when a nation just signs away their sovereignty to join another country, especially in situations where it would never happen in real life. I know we have the realism suggested ideology here, but since we are dealing with real world nations some of the moves seem a bit too contrived.

My 2 cents...

Also, I think we had already agreed on this, but we should have first pick on our nations following a reset. Also I'd be very interesting in never resetting and instead slowly let the game grow into a sci-fi setting.

The only real reason to have a reset it to allow fair gameplay. It's unfair to newer players if the older players have advantages gained through older rules.

As far as "First Pick" goes, we haven't decided yet. It seems like a good idea, but we're worried about it being unfair to newcomers.

However we honestly have no desire to have a community so large as to be unwieldy. Especially until we have bots to automate some things. But that's a thread for another day.

Well yeah I agree that this reset after the rules are finalized makes sense. I meant more after that.

I'd mostly want first pick because I, and I imagine many others, have put a lot of research into our current territories to just abandon them after a shortened game that we didn't realize would be cut short going in, but like you say we can cross that bridge when we come to it.

The [CLAIM] only idea seems like a good one.

"Stricter" can mean many different things. I agree expansions should be a little more realistic - on virtue of better fairness.

Many other online communities allow such a thing as the revolt you mentioned. It's how games like /r/worldpowers can have many more players than their are countries. (That and they have better software to handle regions than we do at this time.) I'm not sure it is feasible for us to track such a thing accurately and fairly until we have bots. We can program bots to do some pretty impressive things, and without them it is a severe handicap to what we are trying to do. This is why I consider the current game to be a "trial" of sorts -we simply can't do much of what we want until we can use our programming skills more fully.

I appreciate your input and we'll see what we can do.
If there is game wipe, I'm afraid I won't be participating anymore.

While I can guarantee there won't be one anytime in the near future, it will happen eventually. It simply is not fair to other players in the long run if there isn't. Most likely when it happens, it will be when we have bots and the rules are in a more solidified state. I'd estimate this to be sometime around six months from now. I'd wager that you change your mind by then.

I can't predict the future, but eventually I won't be doing this and other moderators will take over. They may wipe the game when they do.

It's something that happens, and is expected when you play a game like this.

I'm sorry you feel that way, but eventually it will be in the best interest of the community for the sake of fairness. This is a "game" after all.
